method: PRODUCED - CONSUMED symbol parity (rg across src/, src/bin/, interfaces/, shared/), read-before-write triage

findings.rationale: Field is set to None at all 8 producer sites. Combined with #[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")], the field is never serialized to manifest.json and never read from it either. Survives only as inert struct shape; never observed by Rust code. Round-r4 audit did not flag it.
findings.proposed_change: Option A (recommended): CUT the field. Option B: CONNECT — stamp Utc::now().to_rfc3339() on Github installs and add a doctor check. Option C: leave with FIXME comment.
findings.risk: low — field is None everywhere, removing it cannot change runtime behavior. Only observable difference: operators reading manifest.json no longer see the field (which they cannot today because skip_serializing_if already excludes it).
findings.verification: rg -n installed_at src/ → all hits either declaration or None initializer. rg -n "\.installed_at" src/ → both hits are on hub::origin::OriginEntry, not SkillEntry. After CUT: rg -n installed_at src/bundled/ returns zero.

findings.rationale: Field IS set to Some(BUNDLED_VERSION) for Official skills (extractor.rs:299, 654) and Some(entry.version) for Github-installed skills (hub/install.rs:254). Round-trips through serde. But every .version read across src/ is on a different type (MarketplacePluginEntry or OriginEntry). No Rust code reads bundled::manifest::SkillEntry.version. Doc comment claims intent 'matches bundled_version' which suggests the field was foundation for a never-implemented per-skill upgrade detection.
findings.proposed_change: Option A: DECIDE/leave — keep for future upgrade detection. Option B: CONNECT — add a quick-exit in extract_skills using entry.version == Some(BUNDLED_VERSION). Option C: CUT.
findings.risk: low — field is alive in wire format but inert at behavioral layer. Removing changes on-disk shape of manifest.json only for operators with existing manifests (serde silently drops the field via skip_serializing_if).
findings.verification: rg -n "entry\.version|e\.version|skill\.version" src/ → all hits are on MarketplacePluginEntry or OriginEntry, not SkillEntry. rg -n "\.version" src/bundled/ returns only producer-side construction calls and tests.

findings.rationale: Variant is set in hub/install.rs:253 (production) and hub/install.rs:677 (test). Every behavioral comparison on SkillOrigin either matches Official or constructs Local/Official — no code branch distinguishes Github from Local. Round-r4 BUNDLED-R4-12 noted the same conflation as 'api-design / correctness'. This audit confirms the runtime layer truly never distinguishes them; Github survives only as a serde round-trip label for operators reading manifest.json.
findings.proposed_change: Option A: DECIDE/leave — on-disk distinction has documentary value. Option B: CUT with serde(alias = 'github') on Local so existing manifests still load. Option C: CONNECT — give the variant a behavioral meaning (e.g. skill_manage requires explicit confirmation before removing a Github-sourced skill).
findings.risk: low for A and B (with migration), medium for C (changes user-facing behavior).
findings.verification: rg -n "SkillOrigin::Github" src/ → only writes (hub/install.rs:253, 677), no behavioral match. After CUT with alias: roundtrip test that loads '"source": "github"' deserializes to SkillOrigin::Local.
findings.existing_review_ref: round-r4 BUNDLED-R4-12 (api-design / correctness framing; this audit confirms the behavioral absence)

findings.produced: pub use extractor::SyncReport (name collision with hub::catalog_client::SyncReport)
findings.rationale: Two distinct types share the name SyncReport across module boundaries. bundled::SyncReport is the official-content sync result (bool, bool); hub::catalog_client::SyncReport is the Hub catalog ingestion result (different fields). All call sites use qualified paths so the collision does not produce a compile error, but a reader grepping for SyncReport sees both.
findings.proposed_change: Option A: DECIDE/leave — note the collision in a code comment on each type. Option B: rename bundled::SyncReport → BundledSyncReport and catalog::SyncReport → CatalogSyncReport.
findings.risk: low — collision is cosmetic; either type can coexist with the other.
findings.verification: rg -n "\bSyncReport\b" src/ shows two definitions in disjoint modules. After rename: one definition per module. cargo check -p alephcore compiles.

sanity_check_notes: Cross-checked every pub/pub(crate) item in src/bundled/ against src/, src/bin/, interfaces/, shared/. Every function, struct, enum, and constant has at least one production consumer (documented in REPORT.md cross-checked call sites table). The 4 findings above are the only severed wires in this module — all at the field/variant level, all low-severity, all DECIDE rather than CUT because they round-trip through serde.
